questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should wear a jacket:

options.text: All the time, no matter the weather.
Only if you will ride for more than 30 minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: All the time, no matter the weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding. Even in warm weather, it protects you from the sun and helps prevent dehydration.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast:

options.text: Is safe as long as you stay under the speed limit.
Is safer on a motorcycle than in a car.
Is safe as long as no other vehicles are nearby.
Can make you drift into another lane or off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can make you drift into another lane or off the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. You may not be able to hold the turn and could drift into another lane or off the road. Always slow down before turning.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you properly if:

options.text: You can touch your feet to the ground while sitting on it.
You can reach the controls by stretching.
The handlebars are above your head.
Your feet cannot reach the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can touch your feet to the ground while sitting on it.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you properly if your feet can reach the ground when you are seated. You should also be able to easily reach and use all the controls.

questions.question: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles:

options.text: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
Limits your movement to one area of the lane.
Lets you rely on other drivers to spot hazards.
Forces you to drive faster to keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle gives you time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: During the day, you should:

options.text: Use your headlight only if it is cloudy.
Use your headlight only if you think it helps.

questions.explanation: Always use your headlight, even during the day. This makes other drivers twice as likely to see you.

questions.question: If a driver is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Move to the side of your lane so they can share it.

questions.explanation: The safest way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Change lanes when it is safe and allow them to go ahead. Speeding up will only make things more dangerous.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, the operator should:

options.text: Let air out of the tires to handle the extra weight.
Not tell passengers about upcoming hazards.

questions.explanation: A motorcycle handles differently with a passenger. Keep a larger space cushion between your motorcycle and other vehicles.

questions.question: Which material gives the best protection for motorcyclists?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants provide the most protection when riding.

questions.question: Motorcycles must have all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Nevada law requires motorcycles to have headlights, a red taillight, a brake light, rear reflectors, front and rear brakes, turn signals (if made after 1973), mirrors on both handlebars, fenders on both wheels, footrests, a horn, and a muffler. A flag is not required.

questions.question: Head and neck injuries can be reduced by:
questions.explanation: Wearing a quality helmet greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injuries. A helmet is your best protection in case of an accident.

questions.question: What is the best lane position?

options.text: The one that lets you travel the fastest.
The one that allows you to draft off of other vehicles.
The one that allows other drivers to see you.
The one that places you in other vehicles' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: The one that allows other drivers to see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position where other drivers can see you. A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It also discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if needed. Always try to maximize your space cushion.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles on a motorcycle, you should watch for:

options.text: Motorists looking for a place to park.
Cars pulling away from parking spaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars pulling away from parking spaces.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing parked vehicles. Cars may suddenly pull away from the curb or leave their parking spaces.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you do with your feet?

options.text: It is a good idea to drag your feet.
Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
Keep your feet away from the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests to maintain proper balance. Do not drag your feet on the ground. Do not point your toes downward, as they may catch on the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can reach them quickly if needed.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may show:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. Speed limit signs are rectangular. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When downshifting, what should you do?

options.text: Shift through multiple gears at once.
Shift through one gear at a time.
Always shift all the way down to neutral first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift through one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: When shifting to a lower gear, shift down one gear at a time. Ease out the clutch through the friction zone between each downshift.

questions.question: When braking, which brakes should you use?

options.text: Either brake, but never both at the same time.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time to stop. The brakes work best when used together.

questions.question: The only way to remove alcohol from your body is:
questions.explanation: Only time will remove alcohol from your body. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot speed up this process. There are no shortcuts to sobering up.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should choose shoes with soles that:
questions.explanation: Wear riding boots or shoes that are high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles. Choose footwear with soles made of hard, durable, slip-resistant material.

questions.question: How can you increase your visibility?

options.text: Add auxiliary lights to your motorcycle.
Do not use your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Add auxiliary lights to your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Increase your visibility by wearing bright or reflective clothing. Add auxiliary lights to your motorcycle, use your turn signals, and flash your brake light when appropriate. These actions help other drivers notice you.

questions.question: How can you lower your risk of a crash?

options.text: Tell other road users what you plan to do.
Do not look ahead while riding.
Ride in parts of your lane where you are hard to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other road users what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your turn signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space between you and other vehicles. Always scan the road ahead, behind, and next to you.

questions.question: How should you check tire pressure?

options.text: Look at the tire to see if it looks full.
Squeeze the tire with your hand.
Compare your tire height to another tire.

questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check tire pressure before every ride. A tire that is not full enough may still look okay, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: What does smoothly downshifting on a motorcycle do?

options.text: It lets the engine slow down the motorcycle.
You should not do it around other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets the engine slow down the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Smoothly downshifting lets the engine slow down the motorcycle. This is useful for riders. If you use engine braking, use your brake lights so other drivers know you are slowing down.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions that are coming up.

questions.question: What should you do when riding a motorcycle on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Slow down when riding on slippery surfaces. Use both brakes when you need to stop and avoid sudden movements.

questions.question: How often should you fully check your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: A motorcycle needs to be checked more often than a car. Check your entire motorcycle before each ride.
